insights.summary: Q2 FY27 revenue rose 42.7% to ₹437 Cr with EBITDA of ₹176 Cr (40.3% margin) and PAT of ₹123 Cr. Pharma intermediates grew 53% on CDMO strength while specialty chemicals fell 20% on commodity phase-out and a pause in BFC shipments. Management raised FY27 revenue growth to about 30% (from 25%) and EBITDA margin to 38-40%, pulled the ₹1,000 Cr CDMO target forward to FY27, and set a new ₹2,000 Cr CDMO target for FY30.

what_changed.text: FY27 revenue growth to about 30% from 25%
FY27 EBITDA margin to 38-40% (was similar to FY26's 35.9%)
CDMO ₹1,000 Cr now in FY27, a year early
FY27 capex about ₹300 Cr (was ₹90-95 Cr), including bulk electronic-grade chemicals plant

tone.label: confident
tone.quote: Demand environment remains robust and whatever cost pressures we face due to geopolitical issues, we have been able to pass them on successfully.

analyst_questions.answer: No product-wise numbers; 8-9 products enter the revenue stream over 1-1.5 years and the ₹1,000 Cr is backed by orders already in hand.
Long-term contracts reset prices with raw materials and currency; realisation can rise to the early teens in dollars but not the $30-35 seen in the spot market.
38-40% is for FY27 only; CDMO mix and operating leverage (Ankleshwar at 30% use, battery chemicals very low) support it.
Revenue only from FY28 and small at first while customers qualify the products.

red_flags.text: Working capital stretched to 115 days from 99 days in Q1 because of higher debtor days.
Specialty chemicals revenue down 20% year on year; legacy commodity products still being phased out.
One US customer's acquisition paused BFC shipments in the quarter.
CDMO growth leans on a few large molecules for innovator customers (e.g. Darolutamide); management declined to comment on product-level demand.

watch_next: Q3 revenue and EBITDA margin consistent with 30% growth and 38-40% for the year
First CDMO revenue from the new contracts in H2
Debtor days and working capital falling back
Land acquisition for the next CDMO phase
